key_insight: DK-VLM treats geometry as a first-class signal for spatial reasoning, helping vision-language models better understand 3D relationships across viewpoints. Its Dual-Kernel Attention combines where a token appears in the image with where it is located in the scene, improving spatial judgments as the observer moves.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty vision-language models have in understanding 3D spatial relations across multiple views and updating those relations when the observer changes position. It also tackles the challenge of aligning geometric features from 3D reconstruction with pretrained semantic representations under limited spatial supervision.
method: Introduces Dual-Kernel Attention to compute attention from both the visual token's input position and its geometric position in the reconstructed scene.
Injects 3D geometry into vision-language processing so spatial cues are not limited to 2D image coordinates.
Uses a geometry-aware alignment strategy to better integrate spatial features with existing semantic representations.
impact: This matters for AI practitioners because it improves a model's ability to reason about real-world spatial layouts, which is important for robotics, embodied AI, navigation, and 3D understanding. It also suggests a practical way to combine geometric and semantic cues without requiring heavy spatial supervision.

paper_title: DK-VLM: Geometry as Position for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Han Su, Meng Tian, Tianyu Huang, Mingyu Gao, Lennox Wei
